strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Moves the first objective admission plus drive boundary from caller-side RPC stitching into Rust-owned replay-safe run-control behavior.
Creates the initial task through existing task.start authority and immediately drives the explicit agent loop to a safe stop boundary.
Keeps journey admission, task creation, drive sequencing, replay, and rejection decisions in the Rust runtime rather than the VSIX or caller.
Binds objective admission to bounded progress fingerprints and next-action metadata so a headless caller can recover context from runtime-owned state.
Returns bounded journey metadata and next action derived from runtime progress and completion closure state.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances headless_autonomous_development with supporting agent_loop, runtime_permission_enforcement, persistent_structured_ledger, and progress_visualization.
answers.new_capability: headless.run.drive can accept one explicitly authorized journey admission, create the initial task through existing task.start authority, drive it to the first safe boundary, and replay by journey_id without duplicate task or drive evidence.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: Existing task.start plus headless.run.drive calls leave the cross-RPC objective, task id, session id, drive id, and lost-response recovery boundary outside the runtime.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: A scheduled caller would still need external glue to start and drive a development objective and could duplicate the initial task after a lost response.
answers.non_duplicative: Distinct from M49.3 Mode Pack route dispatch and R7.1/R7.2 control-plane guards; this changes product runtime journey admission behavior.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. The existing headless.run.drive method is extended with bounded journey admission and result metadata.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The phase adds execution/checkpoint metadata, not a report, digest, readiness, history, or inspection surface.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: The Rust runtime validates journey admission, delegates task creation to existing task.start authority, drives the new task through run-control, persists journey checkpoint evidence, replays committed journeys, and rejects invalid or conflicting admission before new side effects.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: A headless controller can start the first golden journey step with one replay-safe runtime call and decide the next action from bounded runtime-owned evidence.
answers.milestone_progress: Establishes the M50 journey identity and admission-to-first-drive model needed for later resume and completion phases.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: M50.1 updates the current and archived phase-value manifests for a product runtime journey-admission phase. Review must confirm the manifest change does not weaken phase-value, product-completion, diagnostics, or source-of-truth enforcement.

exit_criteria: headless.run.drive accepts one bounded journey admission without adding a new RPC
the runtime creates exactly one initial task through existing task.start authority and drives it to a safe stop boundary
journey metadata contains bounded ids, progress fingerprints, closure status, next action, replay flag, and deterministic journey fingerprint
replaying the same journey_id returns persisted bounded metadata without duplicating task, advance, drive, or journey evidence
missing authorization, malformed journey id, raw task-start fields, wrong expected sequence, invalid budget, mixed explicit route target, and conflicting replay fail before creating a new task
VSIX validators accept the bounded journey protocol shape and reject malformed fingerprints or raw/unbounded fields
no report, digest, history, readiness, verdict, inspection, preview, dashboard, generic scheduler, or VSIX-owned policy is added
behavior_evidence: Rust behavior test headless_run_drive_journey_admission_starts_task_drives_and_replays covers authorized task creation, first drive, bounded journey metadata, and replay without additional task creation
Rust behavior test headless_run_drive_journey_denial_fails_before_task_creation covers explicit admission denial before task or checkpoint side effects

Rust behavior test headless_run_drive_journey_invalid_admissions_fail_before_task_creation covers missing authorization, malformed journey id, raw task-start fields, wrong sequence, invalid budget, and mixed route target rejection before task creation
Rust behavior test headless_run_drive_journey_conflicting_replay_fails_without_new_task covers conflicting journey replay rejection without creating another task
VSIX runtimeClient protocol tests accept valid journey params/result metadata and reject false authorization, raw task-start fields, malformed journey fingerprints, and raw journey fields

accepted_capability: Runtime-owned headless development journey admission through existing headless.run.drive
behavior_evidence: cargo test -p brownie-runtime headless_run_drive_journey -- --nocapture passes journey admission, replay, denial, invalid admission, and conflicting replay behavior tests
pnpm --filter brownie-vsix test -- runtimeClient.test.ts passes protocol validator coverage for bounded journey params and results
pnpm --filter brownie-vsix check runs diagnostics, control-plane authority, product-completion, phase-value, and TypeScript checks on the updated manifest and protocol
safety_boundary: reuses existing task.start authority for task creation
journey admission requires explicit authorize=true and authorize_journey_start=true
expected_start_session_sequence must be 0 only for journey admission; normal drive still requires an existing session checkpoint
journey admission cannot mix explicit Mode Pack run-control targets or completion finalization authorization
invalid admission fails before new task creation
RPC and ledger evidence is bounded to ids, counts, enum values, hashes, fingerprints, replay state, and next-action classes
non_goals: no generic workflow engine, scheduler, daemon, or background worker
no automatic apply, recovery, verification retry, provider retry, Mode Pack update, parent join, shell, git, network, or service expansion
no report, digest, history, readiness, verdict, inspection, preview, dashboard, or capability summary surface
rejected_alternatives: caller-side task.start plus headless.run.drive stitching as sufficient
generic internal route executor as the M50.1 deliverable
automatic full Mode Pack update or workspace mutation pipeline
folding R7 guard hardening into this product runtime phase
technical_debt: Task creation still uses UUID-backed task.start; a filesystem failure between task creation and journey checkpoint persistence can leave a task without journey replay evidence and should be considered in a later admission-hardening phase.
The runtime monolith and large test module remain a maintainability risk; module splitting should follow stable behavior slices rather than interrupting M50.1.

External convergence feedback identified future corrective guard work: directory-wide .brownie-control/.codex/tasks authority scanning, direct CI execution of negative guard fixture tests, and stronger finite Product DoD semantics.
M50.1 does not derive later typed routes automatically; a later runtime phase should consider checkpoint-derived next typed target admission under bounded policy.
next_capability_rationale: After M50.1 merges, assess whether M50.2 should resume the same journey across one explicit route boundary or whether a small corrective guard-hardening phase is more urgent.
The next runtime product step should move from caller-provided per-target construction toward runtime-derived next-route admission while preserving existing fail-closed typed authorities.
